Subject: Market index mapping & level translation — proposed deltas

Hey team,

I pulled the localized market indices for EU hubs and attached a draft mapping that translates our current US-centric level midpoints into local equivalents. The goal is to:
- Establish a simple per-level multiplier (index × base midpoint) we can apply consistently across offers
- Flag levels where the current midpoint is materially out-of-line (>12%) with local market medians

Files attached: 20261020_level-mapping-deltas.xlsx (tabs: methodology / raw-indexes / recommended-deltas).

Ask: can you both scan the methodology and the recommended deltas today? Specifically:
- Karthik — sanity-check the percentile we used for L3–L5 (we currently anchor to the 55th percentile; wondering if 60th is justified for sales/SDR roles)
- Marissa — confirm whether the proposed local anchors fit our offer guidelines and whether we should carve a +2% premium for key hiring markets (Dublin, Berlin)

I plan to present a short summary to People Ops and Finance on Friday.

Thanks,
Olga
Principal, Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Olga — useful work. Quick notes from my side after a first pass of the spreadsheet:

- Methodology: OK overall, but please call out which data points are from public job boards vs our CompBench subscription; that changes how I present confidence to Finance.
- Dublin / Berlin premium: +2% seems reasonable for high-demand engineering hires; +3% for senior IC roles (L6+) where supply is tight.
- L3–L5 percentile: prefer keeping 55th for core IC roles; agree to 60th for GTM roles only.

I attached a short PDF with suggested annotated slides and a proposed 3-line summary for Friday. Also: we should add an explicit note on equity strike price assumptions — I got questions in the last hiring review.

Marissa

Good notes. I pulled CompBench raw decile tables for EU markets (attached in the sheet). A couple of thoughts:

- For software engineers L4–L6 I recommend using the 57th percentile as a compromise (reduces oscillation vs 60th but raises competitive offers vs 55th).
- For cost modeling, run a sensitivity at +/- 3% on the local multipliers; that gives Finance a clear cost bucket. I added a new tab (sensitivity) in the workbook.
- For international hires where we expect relocation, hold the local multiplier and add a one-time relocation stipend rather than inflating the midpoint.

I can join the Friday sync to walk the sensitivity outputs if helpful.

—Karthik
Head of Compensation Modeling
Redwood Inference

Folks — couple operational asks before Friday:

1) Can we lock the presentation to a single row per level (US midpoint / local multiplier / resulting local midpoint) — Finance will not want multi-variant slides.
2) For discussion: do we treat EU hubs as separate islands (Dublin/Paris/Berlin) or one EU market with localized premiums? I lean towards islands for L5+ roles.
3) Please add a short bullet on offer policy: "if candidate brings documented competing offer within 10% of our local midpoint, escalate to hiring committee".

I can cover the escalation criteria on Friday. Thanks.
